# Safety bulletin — Airborne dust from blasting (see SB-1007)

This operator note summarizes immediate actions and controls for airborne dust generated during blasting operations. Review SB-1007 in full for background, exposure guidance, and reporting procedures.

Actions before starting work
- Confirm containment enclosures and blast cabinets are intact and seals show no gaps.
- Verify local exhaust and filtration systems are running and filters are serviceable.
- Put up warning signage and ensure bystanders are kept clear.

During operations
- Use approved respiratory protection and eye/face protection whenever dust is present or when working near blasting areas.
- Maintain wet suppression or dust collection at the source when compatible with the job.
- Minimize cleaning with compressed air; use HEPA-filtered vacuums or damp methods for cleanup.
- Stop work and notify supervision if you observe visible dust escaping control systems or if ventilation fails.

Post-operation
- Bag and dispose of spent abrasive per waste handling procedures. Avoid dry sweeping.
- Log equipment issues and replace filters per maintenance protocols.
- Report any symptoms of respiratory irritation to supervision immediately and follow medical reporting steps referenced in SB-1007.

Training and compliance
- Complete the required briefing before performing blasting tasks and attend periodic refresher sessions.
- Supervisors must conduct toolbox talks emphasizing dust controls and PPE.
- Any questions or uncertainties about controls, respirators, or cleanup methods should be raised to safety or maintenance before continuing work.
